issues.description: Animal is specified in the UML/problem statement as having only one attribute "name: String". However, the solution adds an additional attribute "age: int" to Animal, which is not mentioned in the specification. This changes the required state of Animal and implies additional getters/setters beyond what students are instructed to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the model across artifacts: either remove the "age" field (and its getter/setter) from the solution to match the UML/spec, or update the UML/problem statement to include "age: int" and explicitly require its getter/setter.

issues.description: The problem statement implies constructors initialize only the specified attributes (only "name" is specified for Animal), and the template Main.java example instantiates animals with a single String argument (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")). The solution instead requires constructors with two parameters (String name, int age) for Animal and all concrete animals. This mismatch can cause students to implement the wrong constructor signatures and makes the provided template example code incompatible with the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make constructor signatures consistent: either change solution constructors to accept only (String name), or update the problem statement and template Main.java examples to include an age argument everywhere and document it as required.
